title: Another variant of the local criterion of flatness (base change along a square of Noetherian local rings)
statement: Let $R$, $S$, $R'$, $S'$ be Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $\varphi:R\to S$, $\rho:R\to R'$, $\sigma:S\to S'$, $\varphi':R'\to S'$ local homomorphisms (each maps the maximal ideal into the maximal ideal) with $\sigma\circ\varphi=\varphi'\circ\rho$. Let $I\subsetneq R$ be a proper ideal and $I'=IR'$ the ideal of $R'$ generated by $\rho(I)$. Let $M$ be a finitely generated $S$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], an $R$-module through $\varphi$, and $M'=M\otimes_SS'$, an $S'$-module through the second factor and an $R'$-module through $\varphi'$. Assume: (1) the ring map $S\otimes_RR'\to S'$, $s\otimes r'\mapsto\sigma(s)\varphi'(r')$, is a localization of $S\otimes_RR'$ at some multiplicative subset $W$ (every element of $W$ maps to a unit of $S'$; every element of $S'$ is the image of $c$ times the inverse of the image of $w$ for some $c\in S\otimes_RR'$, $w\in W$; and $c\mapsto0$ implies $wc=0$ for some $w\in W$); (2) $M/IM$ is a flat $R/I$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; (3) the homomorphism $\theta:I\otimes_RM\to I'\otimes_{R'}M'$, $a\otimes x\mapsto\rho(a)\otimes(x\otimes1)$, maps the kernel of the multiplication map $I\otimes_RM\to M$, $a\otimes x\mapsto\varphi(a)x$, to zero. (By Remark 00M6 that kernel is $\mathrm{Tor}_1^R(M,R/I)$, the kernel of $I'\otimes_{R'}M'\to M'$ is $\mathrm{Tor}_1^{R'}(M',R'/I')$, and the restriction of $\theta$ is the map of Lemma 00MO (3); so (3) says that this map of Tor groups is zero.) Then $M'$ is a flat $R'$-module.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00MO (lemma-another-variant-local-criterion-flatness, line 23921), with hypothesis (3) on Tor_1 rewritten by Remark Tag 00M6 (remark-Tor-ring-mod-ideal, line 18690: Tor_1^R(M,R/I) = Ker(I (x)_R M -> M)), as in lem-weil-pbc-flat-variant-local-criterion (00ML); the source's proof uses Lemmas 00HI (lemma-flat-base-change), 00ML (lemma-variant-local-criterion-flatness), 00MN (lemma-surjective-on-tor-one-trivial) and 00MM (lemma-surjective-on-tor-one). The identification of the restriction of theta with the Tor map of 00MO (3) is the naturality of the isomorphism of Remark 00M6 (connecting maps of 0 -> I -> R -> R/I -> 0 and 0 -> I' -> R' -> R'/I'), which the split of this node has to write out or replace by a direct kernel argument.
